headline: Eurozone Government Debt Rises to 88.8% of GDP as French Borrowing Costs Climb
summary: Eurozone government debt increased to 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter, with France's debt climbing to 119.1% as benchmark borrowing notes passed 5% amid ongoing political unrest.
why: High sovereign debt-to-GDP ratios and rising bond yields can trigger fiscal crises, elevate borrowing costs for governments, and create volatility in regional currencies and banking stocks.

impacts.name: France
impacts.why: French borrowing costs climbed as benchmark notes passed 5% amid political unrest.

why_moved: Eurozone government debt increased to 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter, driven by climbing French borrowing costs and ongoing political unrest.
